m.d: If you are glad about something, you are happy about it.
m.e: I'm glad to hear you're feeling better.

m.d: If you are glad to do something, you will do it happily.
m.e: "Can you get this door for me?" "Sure, I'd be glad to."

m.d: Glass is a transparent solid and is usually clear. Windows and eyeglasses are made from it, as well as drinking glasses.
m.e: Through the window glass I could see the trees bend in the wind, but I was warm indoors.

m.d: A glass is a drinking cup with no handle.
m.e: As soon as I finished drinking, he filled up my glass again.

m.d: Glasses are worn over the eyes to help you see.
m.e: I've had to wear glasses since I was nine years old.

m.d: Kinds of glass.
If you have glory, you have honour, fame and pride.
If something is global it includes the whole world.
m.e: The weather is changing, and this is not just in one or two places. The change is global.

m.d: Gloria is a female given name.
If something is glorious, it exhibits attributes that are worthy of receiving glory.
A glove is a piece of clothing you wear on your hand to keep your hands warm or safe.
m.e: Police officers often wear gloves when working in crime scenes to avoid destroying evidence.

m.d: Glue is a liquid that pastes items together.
m.e: Can I have some glue to stick my pictures to the paper?

m.d: To glue means to paste something together.
m.e: Your statue broke but I glued it back together.

m.d: A globe is a solid shaped like a ball, often with a map on it.
m.e: He spun the globe on his desk, looking for Japan.

m.d: The globe is the Earth.
m.e: People all around the globe love soccer.

m.d: If something is done gladly, it is done happily or willingly.
A small amount of light.
m.e: The lamp glowed in the dark road.

m.d: A glen is a narrow valley that usually has a river running through it.
m.e: The glen runs through the campsite.

m.d: Glen is a male given name.
(countable) When you catch a glimpse of something, you see it only for a moment.
m.e: I caught a glimpse of baby Prince George as his parents left the hospital.

m.d: To look for a short moment (at something).
m.e: She glanced at her reflection as she passed the mirror.

m.d: If something is glamorous, it is stylish.
If a place is gloomy, it is dark or poorly lit.
m.e: The cavern was gloomy.

m.d: If a person is gloomy, they are unhappy and without hope.
A glitter is a bright, sparkling light.
A glitter is a shiny, decorative material.
If something glitters, it sparkles with light.
Glamour is beauty, charm, and attractiveness.
m.e: She has a glamour that I just can't resist.

m.d: Glamour can be any object that makes someone look better.
Glasgow is a city in Scotland.
A glacier is similar to a mountain or river made of ice.
A glitch is a type of problem that causes a computer program or game to not work properly.
m.e: I don't like glitches because they do a lot of unexpected things that can do damage to my work or game progress.

m.d: A glitch can refer to any type of problem in a computer program or game.
m.e: There is a glitch in this program where the enemy characters can pass through walls in the maze.

m.d: When something glitches, it experiences a problem that causes the computer program to not work properly.
m.e: I am not sure why my computer keeps glitching whenever I run this software.

m.d: To glide is to move without making an effort.
m.e: He glided over the dance-floor.

m.d: To glide is to float in the air gradually downwards.
m.e: When a bird glides, it goes forwards and downward without flapping its wings.

m.d: To glide is to fly in a glider or an aircraft without an engine.
m.e: After losing power, the pilot was able to glide his aircraft to land.

m.d: Gloom means darkness or a feeling of sadness.
A gloss is the shine on a smooth surface.
If you gloss a surface, you make it shiny by applying a glossy substance.
A glare is an angry look.
When you glare at someone, you look at someone angrily.
m.e: I glared at the person that knocked into me just now and making me spill my coffee.

m.d: If a person gloats, they dwell on another's misfortune with malignant pleasure.
A gland is a cell, group of cells, or an organ that makes a special substance, like a hormone.
m.e: The gland that produces sweat is called the sweat gland.

m.d: Glucose is a type of monosaccharide (sugar) found in plants and animals, formula C₆H₁₂O₆.
m.e: Glucose is main source of energy for the body.

m.d: A glimmer is a faint light or glow.
If something glimmers, it shines with a faint, dim light or glow.
If something is glaring, it reflects a lot of light.
A gleaming is a flash of light.
If something is gleaming, it is very bright looking; it is shiny.
Glenda is a female given name.
A sticky liquid used to coat or color something
A smooth edible coating applied to food.
If you glaze windows, you install panes of glass into it.
If you glaze something, you apply a thin layer of coating.
When you gleam, you shine brightly like mirror, with reflected light.
m.e: He gleamed with happiness when he received his examination results.

m.d: To exalt, or give glory or praise to something or someone.
m.e: Fans glorify their favorite divas.

m.d: To make something or someone appear to be more glorious than it or he is.
m.e: Little Rastus' momma glorified his third place win in the kindergarten spelling bee.

m.d: To worship or extol.
m.e: News reporters glorify events barely worth notice.
